movie_characters.description: The charming, fun-loving daredevil of the duo. Veeru is known for his drunken water tank scene, comic timing, and fierce loyalty to Jai.
The brooding, sharp-shooting thinker. Jai is remembered for his quiet demeanor, harmonica theme, and ultimate sacrifice for justice.
The epitome of Bollywood villains. Gabbar’s sadistic charm, iconic laugh, and brutal presence gave India one of its most chilling antagonists.
A tragic ex-cop with no arms, driven by revenge. His stoic silence and moral backbone anchor the story’s justice narrative.
The bold, talkative tonga driver. Basanti’s endless chatter, fearless heart, and chemistry with Veeru made her an instant favorite.
The widow with deep eyes and deeper grief. Radha’s silence, symbolizing loss and love, added poetic depth to the film.
The cowardly yet endearing timber merchant. Known for his exaggerated tales and unique accent, he became a comic legend.
Gabbar’s silent sidekick. With barely a line ('Poore pachaas hazaar!'), Sambha became a cult figure thanks to his menacing aura.
A hapless dacoit who dies in one of Bollywood’s most quoted scenes ('Tera kya hoga Kaalia?'). His fate sealed Gabbar’s ruthlessness.
The moral conscience of Ramgarh. Rahim Chacha’s plea for justice ('Itna sannata kyun hai bhai?') echoed India’s cry for righteousness.
The hilarious Hitler-parody prison warden. His over-the-top salute ('Hum angrezon ke zamaane ke jailer hain!') remains one of the most mimicked lines in Bollywood.
Basanti’s outspoken aunt. Her comical matchmaking scene with Veeru is both iconic and timelessly funny.
